content: 1. The first census in the Netherlands was conducted in 1795, and the last one took place in 197 A law enacted on April 22, 1879, mandated that a census be conducted every ten years. 3. The census scheduled for 1981 was postponed and subsequently canceled. 4. Concerns over privacy led to the cancellation of any further censuses after 1991. 5. In New Zealand, censuses are conducted every five years by Statistics New Zealand (Tatauranga Aotearoa). 6. The most recent census was held on March 7, 2006. 7. For the 2006 New Zealand Census, respondents were given the option to complete their census questionnaires online. 8. In Nigeria, population censuses were conducted during colonial times in 1866, 1871, 1896, 1901, 1911, 1921, and 1952. 9. These censuses primarily covered the southern part of the country, except for the 1952 census, which was nationwide. 10. It is important to note that censuses before 1921 were based on administrative estimates rather than actual enumeration. 11. Post-independence censuses were conducted in 1963, 1973, 1991, and 2006. 12. The results of the 1973 census were highly disputed. 13. Preliminary results from the 2006 census indicated a population of 140,000,000, with 700,000 enumerators involved in the operation. 14. In Norway, the first two male censuses were conducted in the 1660s and 1701. 15. Later statistical censuses were held in 1769, 1815, 1835, 1845, and 1855. 16. Norway’s first nominative and complete census was conducted in 1801, during the rule of the Oldenburg dynasty of Denmark-Norway. 17. The census followed the de jure principle, including military personnel and foreign residents. 18. The 1865, 1875, and 1900 censuses have been digitized and are searchable online. 19. Census records are made publicly available 100 years after their collection. 20. Since 1900, censuses have been conducted every ten years, except for the 1940 census, which was postponed to 1946. 21. Since 2001, the population census has been combined with housing statistics. 22. In Oman, censuses were conducted in 1993 and 2003. 23. The first census in Peru was carried out in 1836. 24. The tenth and most recent census was conducted in 2005 by the Instituto Nacional de Estadística e Informática. 25. The next census was planned for 2007. 26. In Poland, censuses are conducted approximately every ten years by GUS. 27. The most recent census occurred in 2002. 28. The first census in Portugal was conducted in 1864. 29. Censuses in Portugal are carried out every ten years by INE, with the most recent one in 2001. 30. Romania conducted its first census in 1859. 31. Currently, censuses are conducted every ten years by the Institutul Naţional de Statistică (INSSE). 32. The most recent census occurred in 2002. 33. In Russia, the first and only Russian Empire Census was conducted in 1897. 34. The USSR conducted All-Union Population Censuses in 1920 (urban only), 1926, 1937, 1939, 1959, 1970, 1979, and 1989. 35. The first post-Soviet Russian Census was conducted in 2002, with the next one tentatively planned for 2010. 36. The Federal State Statistics Service is currently responsible for conducting censuses in Russia. 37. In Saudi Arabia, population censuses were conducted in 1962/63 (incomplete), 1974 (complete but unreliable), 1992, and 2004. 38. An agricultural census was conducted in 1999. 39. In Serbia, censuses are conducted every ten years, with the most recent one in 2002. 40. The first modern census in Slovenia was conducted in 1991 after independence. 41. The Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia conducted the second census in 2002, with further censuses planned every ten years. 42. The first census in South Africa was conducted in 1911. 43. Several enumerations have occurred since then, with the most recent two conducted by Statistics South Africa in 1996 and 2001. 44. In Spain, censuses are conducted every ten years by INE. 45. The first modern census was conducted in 1768 by Conde de Aranda under the reign of Carlos III. 46. The last four censuses were conducted in 1971, 1981, 1991, and 2001. 47. In Sudan, population censuses were conducted in 1955/56, 1973 (national), 1983 (national), and 1993 (only in the north). 48. A census was planned for February 2008. 49. The first population census in Sweden was conducted in 1749. 50. The last population and housing census was conducted in 1990. 51. Future censuses in Sweden are planned to be based on registers. 52. In Switzerland, the Federal Population Census has been conducted every ten years since 1850. 53. The census was initiated by Federal Councillor Stefano Franscini, who personally evaluated the data from the first census after Parliament failed to provide funding. 54. The Swiss Federal Statistical Office now conducts the census and makes most results available online. 55. Data collected include population data (e.g., citizenship, place of residence, education), household data (e.g., number of individuals in a household), accommodation data (e.g., surface area, rent), and building data (e.g., construction time, number of floors). 56. Participation in the census is compulsory, with a 99.87% participation rate in 2000. 57. Starting in 2010, the census ceased to use written questionnaires distributed nationwide. Instead, data from existing population registers are supplemented with a biannual questionnaire sample of 200,000 people and regular microcensuses. 58. The first population census in Syria was conducted by the French Mandatory Regime in 1921–22, though it is considered unreliable. 59. Censuses during independence were conducted in 1947, 1960 (the first comprehensive demographic investigation), 1970, 1976 (a sample census), 1981, 1994, and 2004. 60. The Turkish census is conducted by Devlet İstatistik Enstitüsü. 61. The first census in Turkey was conducted in 1927. 62. After 1935, censuses were conducted every five years until 1990, after which they have been conducted every ten years. 63. The most recent census was in 2000. 64. Census enumeration in Turkey takes place on a single day, unlike other countries where it takes 1–2 weeks. 65. Approximately 900,000 enumerators were involved in the 2000 census. 66. The 15th census, based on improved geographical information systems, was planned for 2010. 67. A census was conducted in the Ottoman Empire between 1831 and 1838 by Sultan Mahmud II as part of the Tanzimat reform movement. 68. Even Christian and Jewish men were counted, but women were excluded. 69. The first censuses in Uganda were conducted in 1911, 1921, and 1931, using primitive methods. 70. Enumeration units were huts rather than individuals. 71. More scientific censuses were conducted in 1948 and 1959, with persons as the enumeration unit. 72. These censuses were divided into separate enumerations for Africans and non-Africans. 73. Post-independence censuses in 1969, 1980, and 1991 were conducted jointly for all races. 74. The 1980 and 1991 censuses included housing information and a larger questionnaire for a sample of the population. 75. The questionnaires for the 1980 census were lost, and only provisional figures are available from this census.
